title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
slides: PSI wants to turn discovery into a business model
But science rarely fits a product cycle
Their platform sells discovery-as-a-service to labs
Few buyers can price an unknown result upfront
Ask: who actually pays when the science fails?
thread_text:
1. The real bill for discovery

PSI sells discovery-as-a-service to labs, but when a result is unknown, few buyers can price it upfront. So who covers the cost when the science fails?

2. Science vs. product cycle

Research rarely fits a product cycle. PSI's model assumes it can, turning unpredictable discovery into a repeatable business.

3. Labs buy, but can they price?

Labs are the customers, yet an unknown result has no sticker price. That mismatch is the hidden risk in PSI's platform.

4. Discovery as a service

PSI's platform sells discovery-as-a-service, but if buyers can't price the unknown, the service may stall before it scales.

5. Who pays when science fails?

Ask yourself: if you were a lab, would you pay upfront for a result that might never come? That's the question PSI must answer.

instagram.caption:
Labs are being sold "discovery as a service" — but an unknown result has no sticker price.

PSI wants to turn scientific discovery into a repeatable business model, selling its platform to labs as a service. 🔬

The problem: research rarely fits a product cycle, and few buyers can price a result upfront when nobody knows what it will be.

If you write or publish about science, this is the model to watch — and question. ⚠️

If you ran a lab, would you pay upfront for a result that might never come? 💭
